name: Partner Specific Trust Can Lag Relational Change
text: The heightened mutual trust needed for inclusive and unmediated coordination is not shown to be better inference, higher reward, or prompt updating after conduct changes. In multi-partner graded trust-game simulations, partner-specific confidence can sharpen policy commitment without necessarily producing higher rewards or directly improving partner-state inference, and accumulated confidence can remain behaviorally active after a partner's conduct changes. This is an analogical qualification of the claim, not a finding about firms.
scope_conditions: The position is Kaal's own cross-domain application of the cited claim; the source's authors do not make it.
The source passage is taken from the arXiv abstract; the full paper was not reviewed.
Analogical qualification only; not evidence about firms, boards, or unmediated corporate governance.
